card.title: Earthworm — Excretory, Nervous and Reproductive Systems

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The earthworm's internal systems are well adapted to its soil-dwelling life. The digestive system (buccal cavity → crop → gizzard → intestine with typhlosole) processes decaying matter. The closed circulatory system has 5–6 heart-like vessels. The excretory system uses metanephridia (intersegmentary, septal, genital). The nervous system (cerebral ganglion + ventral nerve cord) coordinates peristaltic movement.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Digestive: buccal → pharynx → oesophagus → crop → gizzard → intestine (typhlosole) → rectum → anus
Nephridia: intersegmentary + septal + genital
Circulatory: dorsal vessel → 5–6 hearts → ventral vessel → capillaries (closed)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Earthworms have a CLOSED circulatory system (blood in vessels), not open.  ·  The crop STORES food; the gizzard GRINDS it (like a chicken's gizzard) — they are different organs.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects labelled diagrams of the digestive, excretory, and reproductive systems.  ·  The typhlosole (intestine fold) and the crop/gizzard distinction are common exam points.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Crop (bulbous storage) and gizzard (muscular grinding) — like a chicken's crop and gizzard.  ·  Typhlosole: an internal ridge in the intestine that doubles the absorptive area.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Nephridia types: intersegmentary (perivisceral) connect two segments; septal are at septa; genital in the clitellum region.  ·  Earthworms are hermaphrodites but STILL cross-fertilise (exchange sperm with a partner).

rows.label: Derivation

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Digestive: C-G-T (Crop store, Gizzard grind, Typhlosole absorb).  ·  Circulatory = CLOSED (blood in vessels).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Digestive system (crop, gizzard, typhlosole)  ·  Nervous system  ·  Excretory (metanephridia)  ·  Closed circulatory system

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Digestive: crop (store) + gizzard (grind) + typhlosole (absorb).  ·  Nervous: cerebral ganglion + ventral nerve cord + segmental ganglia.  ·  Excretory: metanephridia (intersegmentary, septal, genital).  ·  Circulatory: closed system; 5–6 heart-like vessels.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The typhlosole (internal fold of the intestine) increases absorptive surface area.  ·  The cerebral ganglion ("brain") sits above the oesophagus; the ventral nerve cord runs the length of the body.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Describe the nervous system of the earthworm.  ·  Explain copulation and cocoon formation in earthworms.  ·  State the economic importance of earthworms.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Describe the nervous system.  ·  Explain copulation and cocoon formation.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Nephridia: intersegmentary, septal, and genital types.  ·  Copulation: two worms form a loop, exchange sperm, then the clitellum secretes a cocoon containing the fertilised eggs.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: The grinding organ in the earthworm is the: → B  ·  The internal fold that increases the intestine absorptive area is the: → C

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Digestive system: buccal cavity → pharynx → oesophagus → crop (storage) → gizzard (grinding) → intestine (with typhlosole for increased surface) → rectum → anus.  ·  Nervous system: cerebral ganglion (brain) above the oesophagus; ventral nerve cord (double sub-oesophageal ganglion) with segmental ganglia; sensory organs in prostomium.  ·  Excretory system: metanephridia (nephridia) — one pair per segment; types: integmentary (perivisceral), septal, and genital; collect coelomic fluid and excrete ammonia/urea.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Hermaphroditic reproduction  ·  Copulation and cocoon  ·  Economic importance

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Reproductive: hermaphrodite; cross-fertilisation; clitellum forms cocoon.  ·  Economic: soil aeration, humus, bioremediation, soil health indicator.  ·  The ventral nerve cord is the main nerve structure; the cerebral ganglion (brain) is above the oesophagus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Excretion: earthworms excrete ammonia (urea) in moist environments; they do NOT produce urea like mammals in large amounts.  ·  Nephridia types (intersegmentary, septal, genital) are a frequent short-answer.  ·  Copulation and cocoon formation are a favourite long-answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Learn the digestive pathway (buccal to anus).  ·  Differentiate crop (storage) and gizzard (grinding).  ·  List the three types of nephridia.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The crop stores food; the gizzard grinds it; the typhlosole increases absorption.  ·  Earthworms have a closed circulatory system with heart-like vessels.  ·  Metanephridia are the excretory organs of annelids.
